summary: User identified need for native Puppet Master Goal Mode because Codex Goal Mode succeeded where prompt-packet ledger transfer failed, and PM users will use multiple model providers/qualities.

Captured implementation lessons from Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode plugins, and PI goal projects: durable state, continuation scheduling, constrained tools, evaluator/judge loops, and limitations of hook/marker approaches.

Captured risk that low-quality agents may miss or hallucinate issues in massive documents; design requires runtime-owned completion, evidence/certification, role separation, and bounded worker authority.
Captured requirement that invisible internal Goal Mode must be completely hands-off except explicit user stop/constraint or true hard blockers.
User corrected earlier framing: old prompt-packet/D2 approach did not work and should not be preserved as foundation; native Goal Mode must preserve whole-task coherence.
Reviewed current repo planning substrate: standardized v2 ledgers, standardized Plan docs/PlanUnits, current Chain Wizard docs incomplete, and node compiler contract intentionally incomplete.
Captured user-facing Goal Mode UI requirements: activation button/chip, /goal, natural language activation, status indicator, tasks/todos, pause/resume/stop, goal update controls, and status menu.
Captured requirement for parent goals to spawn parallel agents/child goals with dedicated objectives and synthesize results under parent authority.
Captured Codex v0.140.0 Goal Mode attachment preservation requirement for oversized text, large pasted blocks, images, and remote app-server sessions.

Captured PMConcept assistant-chat surfaces that Goal Mode should reuse: mode dropdown, slash menu, plan/task tracker, thread pulse/summary, footer context usage, active subagent indicator, files-touched strip, message blocks, and runtime popovers.
Materialized retrospective v2 planning ledger for Native Goal Runtime and Assistant Chat Goal Mode, ready for a later explicit compile to canonical Plans.

Validated generated ledger package with `python3 scripts/pm-bootstrap-ledger-validate.py Plans/ledgers/v2/pldg-20260616-001-goal-runtime-system`; validation passed with zero errors and zero warnings. Full governance gates were not run as a package requirement because this active ledger intentionally does not update Spec Lock, evidence bundles, shards, plan_graph, auto_decisions, or other governance seal artifacts.

Jared resumed the Goal Runtime/System ledger for conversational refinement, explicitly not a Goal run and not a compile. No new canonical Plans, generated governance artifacts, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, design atoms, decisions, blockers, or recorded open questions were created by the resumption itself; the next turn should answer or refine the assistant's pre-compile clarification prompts, or explicitly request compile.

Captured Jared's pre-compile hardening choices: risk- and phase-tiered Goal Completion Receipts, explicit Goal Replan Events for material mid-goal changes, first-class collapsible child goals, phase-bound snapshots for evidence/certification, and child-goal write-authority policies. The ledger remains ready for explicit compile and no canonical Plans or generated governance artifacts were written.

Captured Jared's requirement that the Settings GUI expose separate Goal Mode model selections: one worker model and one verifier/adjudicator model. This refines the model-role policy surface without resolving provider-specific default tier mappings. No canonical Plans or generated governance artifacts were written.

Jared asked whether anything else needs to be figured out for implementation readiness. Assessment: no hard blockers were identified and the ledger remains ready for explicit compile. Recommended optional final policy defaults before compile are verifier/adjudicator setting fallback semantics, provider-neutral escalation triggers, user approval boundaries for high-risk operations, verifier failure/degraded-mode behavior, and completion receipt evidence retention/redaction. These are implementation-hardening questions, not blockers unless Jared chooses to make them required before compile.

Jared locked final implementation policy defaults before compile: verifier/adjudicator inheritance is allowed only when the inherited worker model satisfies the goal certification tier policy; escalation triggers include stale/non-replayable evidence, child-output conflicts, repeated retries/blockers, strong-certification surfaces, destructive/governance actions, low worker confidence, out-of-scope writes, validator failures, and unsupported completion claims; verifier unavailable behavior is tiered; explicit approval is required for high-risk authority boundaries; evidence retention keeps hashes/summaries/artifact identities while capping/redacting raw logs; and child direct writes require isolated worktree, explicit non-overlapping scope, or parent-granted single-writer lease. No canonical Plans or generated governance artifacts were written.

Final readiness assessment confirmed no additional hard blockers before compile. The ledger is implementation-ready for compile to canonical Plans: core Goal Runtime architecture and safety policy surfaces are captured, final policy defaults are accepted, no open blockers or open questions remain, and the remaining deferred questions are non-blocking integration/implementation details to represent in Plans. No canonical Plans or generated governance artifacts were written.

Follow-up readiness check reconfirmed that no additional hard blockers are needed before implementation-ready compile. The remaining useful items are compile-time representation details and deferred implementation choices already captured as non-blocking questions: Chain Wizard final flow, PlanUnit-to-Node compiler contract, final Goal UI styling, persistence substrate, and provider-specific model tier defaults. No canonical Plans, generated governance artifacts, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, or executable queues were written.

Aligned deferred question q-0005 with the compact open-items projection by adding atom-0104 and atom-0105 to its linked_atom_ids and preserving the accepted separate worker/verifier-adjudicator selector and certification-tier verifier policy as settled decisions. This is a ledger lineage cleanup only; it does not add a new open question or design blocker. No canonical Plans, generated governance artifacts, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, or executable queues were written.

Assessed implementation readiness after locking tiered certification, verifier/adjudicator model requirements, escalation triggers, verifier-unavailable behavior, approval boundaries, evidence retention, and child write-authority policy defaults. No additional product-level blockers were identified. Remaining deferred questions are implementation-owner or future-compiler choices, not blockers to starting implementation planning.
